title: The SBA Just Rolled Over on Rollover Equity

 The SBA Just Rolled Over on Rollover Equity
Sara,
Heads up, buyers and sellers—especially the ones eyeing a little equity rollover in your next deal.
The SBA’s latest revision to SOP 50 10 8 (effective June 1, 2025) just dropped, and it comes with a curveball that could change the way deals are structured.
Here’s the big news:
If a seller keeps any equity—yes, even 1%—they now have to personally guarantee the entire SBA 7(a) loan. Not just their sliver of the pie. The whole thing. And that personal guarantee sticks around for two years after the deal closes.
Previously, this only kicked in if you owned 20% or more. So yes, this is a big shift. One that could make some sellers think twice before hanging onto a small piece of the business.
What does this mean for deals?
Well, we’re likely going to see:
More caution with rollover equity. If you thought you’d keep a toe in the water without getting soaked—surprise! You're swimming in the deep end now.

A stronger push for outside capital. Think investor-backed deals, seller notes structured outside SBA guidelines, or other creative financing workarounds.

This also means SBA lenders are going to be extra nosy about your deal structure. So if you're the buyer, make sure your legal and lending teams are in sync. And if you’re the seller—know what you’re signing up for.
Of course, we’ve seen SOPs evolve before. It’s entirely possible this gets softened or reinterpreted later. But for now, this is theoretically going to be the rule. 
Need help navigating SBA rules or deal structuring? That’s kind of our thing.
Until next time—make smart deals and skip the surprises,
Sara Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
Business Consultant & Founder of Deal Academy
